summary: The two grids a product page is made of — tiles that auto-fill, charts that step 1 → 2 → 3 on the content column.
structureFrom: Content width — wide screens (the 1920 and 2560 frames)
measurementsFrom: docs/foundations/responsive.md and the Layout and breakpoints story

pairs.dont: Write grid grid-cols-tiles gap-gutter, or grid-cols-1 @3xl:grid-cols-2 @7xl:grid-cols-3, by hand on a page.
pairs.why: The rule used to live only in a sentence, so every product re-derived it and could drift without anyone noticing. A rule in a component is a rule that runs.

pairs.dont: Reach for xl: or 2xl: inside the content column.
pairs.do: Let the grid answer to its container.
pairs.why: The viewport knows nothing about the rail, the page padding, a width cap or an open drawer. The same grid gets 976 at a 1280 viewport with the rail open and 1184 with it collapsed, so a viewport breakpoint is wrong at the width the grid was actually given.

pairs.dont: Put a table or a time series in a ChartGrid.
pairs.why: Tables and time series take the full row at every width — they are not one of three columns, they are the row. A cell that must always span every column is not a cell.

pairs.dont: Give the grid an aspect ratio so the charts scale with it.
pairs.do: Give the chart a fixed height range, 240–320.
pairs.why: An aspect ratio makes a chart grow tall on a wide screen, which nobody asked for. The grid sets columns and gap; height is the chart's own business.

a11y: Both are presentational containers — they add no role and no landmark, so the tiles and cards inside keep whatever semantics they came with.
Column count changes with the container, not with a media query, so a zoomed page reflows the same way a narrow one does. Reflow at 400% is a container question here, which is the point.
